title: Impact of ChatGPT on Learning Motivation: Teachers and Students' Voices
venue: Journal of English Studies in Arabia Felix
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether ChatGPT influences English language learning motivation, with particular attention to perceived effects on language skill development. Rather than testing achievement gains with an experimental design, the authors surveyed teachers and students shortly after ChatGPT became publicly available and asked for their views on its motivational impact.

The study used a quantitative questionnaire administered online to 80 participants drawn from English-language teachers/instructors and students. The instrument asked about ChatGPT’s perceived effects on macro-skills (listening, speaking, reading, writing), micro-skills (grammar, vocabulary), and motivation-related dimensions such as autonomy, self-confidence, interest, fun/enjoyment, interaction, and career-oriented motivation. Participants were geographically dispersed and responded via email and WhatsApp; the study appears to have been conducted in the early months of 2023 in Saudi Arabia-based institutions, with some author affiliations also in Yemen and India.

Findings were broadly positive. Respondents believed ChatGPT was especially motivating for reading, writing, grammar, and vocabulary, while views on listening and speaking were neutral. The strongest perceived motivational effects were on vocabulary, independent learning, and fun/enjoyment. ANOVA results indicated differences by teaching experience for perceptions of ChatGPT’s effects on listening and interest in learning English, with more experienced participants more likely to see benefits. The paper concludes that ChatGPT is viewed as a motivational tool for English learning, but it does not provide direct evidence of literacy outcome gains against a non-AI or business-as-usual comparison.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI conversational chatbot / large language model tool for dialogue, text generation, and assistance across tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a newly launched chatbot in English language learning; participants reported perceptions of how ChatGPT affects motivation and language-skill development.

findings.finding_summary: This paper reports teacher and student perceptions (n=80) that ChatGPT motivates EFL learners to develop reading and writing skills, with mean ratings of 4.02 (SD 1.0905) for reading and 3.92 (SD 1.01601) for writing. Participants were neutral on listening (M=3.32, SD 1.2806) and speaking (M=3.25, SD 1.2877), and also viewed ChatGPT favorably for vocabulary (M=4.45, SD 0.6731) and grammar (M=3.92, SD 0.9648).
findings.measure: Likert-scale questionnaire ratings of perceived impact on reading, writing, listening, speaking, grammar, and vocabulary

findings.finding_summary: Participants generally agreed that ChatGPT increases motivation-related outcomes including autonomy (independent learning M=4.025, SD 0.826385), self-confidence (M=3.975, SD 0.826385), fun/enjoyment (M=4.0, SD 0.954669), interest in learning English (M=3.55, SD 1.123962), interaction with others (M=3.875, SD 0.932874), and eagerness to get a job (M=4.0, SD 0.871489). The paper interprets these responses as positive expectations for ChatGPT's motivational effects.
findings.measure: Likert-scale questionnaire ratings of motivation-related constructs

findings.finding_summary: ANOVA found significant differences by teaching experience for perceived listening-skill impact (F=4.57817, p=0.0132231) and interest in learning English (F=8.04608, p=0.00067103). Tukey post hoc tests showed high-experience participants differed significantly from low-experience participants on listening (mean difference=1.21429, p=0.009), while effects on interest were significant for high-experience versus low-experience and high-experience versus students (mean differences 0.92857 and 0.87218, both p=0.001).
findings.measure: ANOVA and Tukey HSD comparisons of perceived effects by teaching experience
findings.confidence_interval: 95% CI for listening high vs low: 0.255 to 2.1735; interest high vs low: 0.3331 to 1.5241; interest high vs students: 0.3034 to 1.441

quality_tier_rationale: This is a cross-sectional perception study using a questionnaire, not an intervention or causal evaluation. It provides descriptive and inferential evidence about attitudes toward ChatGPT, but no direct outcome gains for reading or literacy.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports positive perceived effects on reading and writing, with the strongest mean rating for vocabulary, but these are not measured learning gains and effect sizes for literacy outcomes are not reported. Evidence for direct K-12 reading/literacy improvement relative to business-as-usual is therefore unclear and modest at best.
